prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: use a listings/knowledge‑graph management service — Yext is the single best commercial product for making sure AI assistants (including services that draw on knowledge graphs and OpenAI integrations) can find and recommend your business. 

Why Yext:
- It syncs your name, address, phone, hours, categories, and rich attributes across search engines, maps, voice assistants and many AI platforms.
- Yext has integrations and partnerships aimed at AI assistants and knowledge graphs, so it’s designed to surface your business to tools that generate recommendations.
- It also provides monitoring and analytics so you can see where your info is being used.

Free and lower‑cost essentials you should also do:
- Claim and optimize Google Business Profile (most important for discovery)
- Claim Bing Places and Apple Maps / Maps Connect
- List on major review sites (Yelp, TripAdvisor, Facebook) and data aggregators (Foursquare, Infogroup)
- Add LocalBusiness schema (structured data) on your website so crawlers and models can read your details
- Encourage reviews and keep hours/contact details accurate

How to check if ChatGPT (and similar AIs) recommend you:
- Test directly in ChatGPT with web access / browsing or with the “web_with_bing” tool: ask prompts like “Recommend a [your service] in [city]” and “Why should I choose [your business name]?”
- Use Yext / Uberall /BrightLocal /Moz Local to scan where your listings appear and what data is published
- Search in Google, Bing, Apple Maps, and voice assistants (Siri/Alexa) — many AIs base answers on those sources

Other vendors to consider:
- Uberall, BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark (local SEO/listings monitoring)
- For larger custom integrations: build an OpenAI ChatGPT plugin or provide a public API/knowledge base so ChatGPT (when using plugins or browsing) can reference your authoritative data

Quick action plan:
1) Claim Google Business Profile and verify.
2) Add LocalBusiness schema to your site and a clear “About” page.
3) Use Yext (or Uberall/BrightLocal) to push consistent listings to directories and monitor them.
4) Get reviews and add unique content (photos, menus, service pages).
5) Test in ChatGPT with browsing/plugins enabled and in voice assistants.

If you want, tell me your city and business type and I’ll suggest the exact search prompts to test and the top platforms you should claim.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
